relevance_note: The paper describes one kindred in which three sisters with fish-eye disease are compound heterozygous for LCAT T123I and an intron 4 branchpoint mutation: "Sequencing of the LCAT gene of all three probands revealed compound heterozygosity".
method_note: Read the paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and took table-row spans by slicing the paper's own Table I/II lines (checked against the tables). Scope: 17 family members listed in Table I by pedigree label (3 compound heterozygous sisters III-2, III-5, III-6; 5 T123I heterozygotes; 3 intron-mutation heterozygotes; 6 relatives listed as 'Normal' i.e. tested negative by DNA analysis). Labels are the paper's own pedigree labels. The 52-year-old female index patient (abdominal pain, constipation, normal endoscopy, treated for irritable bowel disease, RT-PCR on her leukocytes) is one of III-2/III-5/III-6, but the text does not say which (only the pedigree figure arrow, not available as text); her individual facts (age 52, abdominal pain, constipation, treatment) are therefore not assigned to any row and no extra row was created. Contradiction: the Results text says 'we identified four T123I carriers within the same family' while Table I/II list five subjects heterozygous for T123I (III-1, III-3, IV-1, IV-2, IV-3); the table was followed. Features of the sisters (corneal opacities, low HDL-c, low apo A-I, high apo B, elevated TG, LCAT activity/concentration) come from statements naming the three sisters/probands, with per-person Table I/II values as detail; reduced LCAT concentration not recorded for III-6 (Table II 'nd'). Heterozygote LCAT activity rows come from the group statement naming heterozygotes for either mutation; III-1 left out (Table II all 'nd'); III-9 recorded as excluded from the statement that she/he had low normal LCAT activity. 'Low normal HDL-cholesterol and apo A-I' in heterozygotes, and group-mean comparisons of TC/LDL-c/apo B in T123I carriers, were not turned into per-person checklist statuses (III-10's HDL-c is 0.56, so 'low normal' is not clearly true for every member). Premature atherosclerosis recorded as excluded for all 17 from 'None of the three sisters nor their family members were known to suffer from premature atherosclerosis' (hedged 'known to'); the broader checklist item 'atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease' left not reported. Variant nomenclature is legacy: T123I (mature-protein numbering, nucleotide 'C 2182 to T') and IVS4:T-22C ('T 2327 to C'); no c./p./transcript printed, so cdna/protein HGVS fields hold only the printed protein shorthand. Variant type of the intronic branchpoint mutation recorded as 'other' (authors call it an intronic/branchpoint point mutation causing intron retention, not a splice-site variant). Inheritance left 'not reported': the paper says the T123I defect 'originated from the father's side of the family' and the intron mutation carriers are in 'the other branch of the pedigree', but no parent is stated to carry either variant. Sex of relatives not stated in text (only in the pedigree figure). Table I header units ('mmol/liter' on every column) are as printed.

span: we could not detect LCAT activity nor LCAT mass in the culture medium harvested from the LCAT-Int4-MUT cell line

this gene defect was shown to cause a null allele as the result of complete intron retention
